question: What is the air quality in Singapore right now?
name: Claude
answer:
Singapore's air quality is currently **unhealthy, and very unhealthy in the west**. The latest reading I found is from the National Environment Agency (NEA), via CheckpointSG, as of 15 Oct, 1:00 pm.

| Region | 24-hr PSI | Band | 1-hr PM2.5 (µg/m³) |
|---|---|---|---|
| West (Tuas) | 210 | Very Unhealthy | 139 |
| Central | 194 | Unhealthy | 152 |
| East | 170 | Unhealthy | 146 |
| South | 162 | Unhealthy | 134 |
| North (Woodlands) | 128 | Unhealthy | 98 |

- **Advice:** NEA's guidance is to avoid strenuous outdoor activity. Elderly people, pregnant women, children and anyone with heart or lung disease should avoid outdoor activity altogether.
- **Cause:** The Star reported that smoke haze is drifting in on south-easterly winds. Dry conditions are forecast to continue over parts of southern Sumatra and Kalimantan.
- **Outlook:** NEA forecast that PSI would stay in the unhealthy range for the 24 hours after its 13 Oct evening advisory. This year's peak so far was a PSI of 192 in the central region on 9 Oct.

PSI bands are Good (0–50), Moderate (51–100), Unhealthy (101–200), Very Unhealthy (201–300) and Hazardous (above 300).

These readings update hourly. For the latest, check the NEA website or the myENV app.

Air quality in Singapore https://www.iqair.com/singapore None
Studies have shown that there is a link between high Pollution Standards Index (PSI) levels and an increased short-term risk to mortality.1 As a city-state, air pollutants primarily come from traffic and industry year-round but there is also a seasonal risk, posed by haze from forest fires in neighbouring island states.2 Severe haze events can cause an increase in hospital admissions due to respiratory illnesses but severe haze events are uncommon and all haze events are short term in their nature.2 Routine haze events can have a minimal impact on air quality and Singapore’s Ministry of Health advises that residents continue with activities as normal unless the PSI rises above 100.3 Otherwise, Singapore experiences a similar incidence of adverse impacts on public health from air pollution, as many North American and European cities, such as Prague air quality and Berlin air pollution.2  What is the PSI level in Singapore?    The Singapore air quality index is the Pollution Standards Index (PSI) – it is an alternative to the Air Quality Index (AQI) that is used in Singapore. Many other countries now commonly use their own versions of an Air Quality Index as a common metric for air quality but Singapore’s National Environment Agency (NEA) uses a variant PSI, which was devised by the United States Environmental Protection Agency.
